key_insight: COSMA co-optimizes fermion mapping, Pauli scheduling, and qubit allocation to cut inter-core communication in modular quantum simulation.
engineering_relevance: The work directly targets a key scalability bottleneck in multi-core quantum hardware, improving the practicality of chemistry and other fermionic simulations.
method: Qubit allocation and Pauli scheduling to reduce state transfers
evidence_signal: On molecular benchmarks, COSMA reports up to 2.5x lower communication cost than state-of-the-art baselines, with a 1.7x median improvement.
watch_item: Benefits depend on the modular hardware model and compiler assumptions, so real-device gains may vary with connectivity, noise, and routing overhead.
paper_title: COSMA: Communication-aware Optimization of Fermionic Simulation Kernels for Modular Quantum Architectures
